question: Was the apparent early-EndTurn log-probability deficit a candidate-label or legal-action bug, and did the teacher voluntarily end turns before exhausting actions?
method: Replay every exported complete-turn candidate on fit maps. Verify that its final locally indexed action is the unique legal EndTurn and that the replayed post-turn state matches the native export. At teacher and static pre-EndTurn states, count all other legal actions, their types, ready owned units and owned treasury. Compare native immediate static scores and searched three-turn followup scores for the two candidate plans.
interpretation: The native export and local action labels agree. Most selected early EndTurns are genuine optional choices with many remaining legal actions; the static rank-zero plan usually ends only after alternatives are exhausted.

A forced static EndTurn has model probability one by legal-action masking. Contrasting its log probability with an optional teacher EndTurn, as in the prior fit-only margin report, mostly compares different choice sets and cannot by itself diagnose a defective stop policy.

The teacher usually gives up immediate static score for a higher searched followup score. The latter is selected by the search objective, so this is not independent evidence of terminal benefit or a causal explanation of the validated complete-game gain.
The rejected student remains rejected: its independent offline gate failed. No inference policy, rating, browser bot or game rule changed.
verification: Remote one-core nice19 Python: 417 tests passed, Ruff check and format clean. All 236 selected and static complete-turn plans replayed and final EndTurn local indices validated.
qualification: Exploratory read-only analysis on already-used fit maps. Candidate states are correlated. Search followup scores are conditional heuristic values, not terminal outcome labels, Elo or evidence that any student improved.
